1451.subject: Physics
1451.text: Assertion: Gauss's law can't be used to calculate electric field near an electric dipole. Reason: Electric dipole don't have symmetrical charge distribution.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1451.sol: Gauss's law is applicable for any closed surface. Gauss's law is most useful in situation where the charge distribution has spherical or cylindrical symmetry or is distributed uniformly over the plane. Whereas electric dipole is a system of two equal and opposite point charges separated by a very small and finite distance.

2013.subject: Zoology
2013.text: Assertion : Less iodine intake causes goitre. Reason : Less iodine in body decreases thyroxine secretion.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
2013.sol: (a) : Simple goitre or endemic goitre is the enlargement of thyroid gland accompanied with cretinism or myxoedema. It occurs in case of hyposecretion of thyroxine. To compensate for lower secretion of thyroxine from cells, thyroid gland enlarges to accommodate more secretory cells. It is caused due to dietary deficiency of iodine. To form normal quantities of thyroxine about 1 mg / week of ingested iodine is required in the form of iodides.

2092.subject: Zoology
2092.text: Assertion : Mammalian ova produces hyaluronidase. Reason : The eggs of mammal are microlecithal and telolecithal.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2092.sol: Hyaluronidase, a hydrolytic enzyme is an acrosomal content in mammalian sperm. It helps at the time of fertilization during the penetration of sperm into ovum. Based on the amount of yolk mammalian eggs are alecithal means egg without yolk. Microlecithal eggs are with very little yolk e.g., sea urchin, starfish. On the basis of distribution of yolk telolecithal eggs are those eggs in which the yolk is concentrated towards the vegetal pole and cytoplasm and nucleus lie near the animal pole e.g., birds and reptiles.

2284.subject: Zoology
2284.text: Assertion : Connective tissue inside the brain is essential for conduction of nerve impulse. Reason: Connective tissue hold together the nerve cells of brain.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2284.sol: Connective tissue consists of variously shaped cells lying in an extracellular material called matrix. It joins one tissue to another in the organs. Connective tissue is absent inside the central nervous system i.e. brain and spinal cord and thus has no function in the conduction of nerve impulse.The nerve cells of the brain and spinal cord are held together by supporting cells called neuroglia cells.

Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum, lumbar vertebra
Sacrum, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, cervical vertebra
Cervical vertebra, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum
84725.sol: The vertebral column of humans is divided into different regions. 124770.subject: Botany

Speeds up the malting process in the brewing industry

The metabolic pathway through which the electron passes from one carrier to another, is called the electron transport system (ETS) (Figure 12.4) and it is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane .

In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. This stage of endosperm development is called free-nuclear endosperm. 126164.subject: Botany
126164.text: Parts of Monocot embryo Location/Features A. Coeleptile 1. Hollow foliar structure B. Coelrrhiza 2. Lateral side of embryonal axis C. Scutellum 3. Inside an undifferentiated sheath D. Root cap 4. Encloses radical
126164.sol: Embryos of monocotyledons (Figure 1.14 b) possess only one cotyledon. In the grass family the cotyledon is called scutellum that is situated towards one side (lateral) of the embryonal axis. At its lower end, the embryonal axis has the radical and root cap enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called coleorrhiza. The portion of the embryonal axis above the level of attachment of scutellum is the epicotyl. Epicotyl has a shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure, the coleoptile.

126178.subject: Botany

126178.sol: Flowers that are small, closed flowers with unexposed reproductive organs are called Cleistogamous flowers.

126274.subject: Botany
126274.text: A farmer sows seeds collected from his high-yielding hybrid crop to raise the next generation of plants. However, he observes that the new plants have lost their high yield and other desired traits. Which of the following biological phenomena, if introduced into the hybrid crop, would prevent this loss of traits in subsequent generations?
126274.sol: Sowing seeds collected from hybrid plants normally leads to the segregation of traits due to meiosis and fertilization during sexual reproduction, causing a loss of hybrid vigor. Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction by producing seeds without fertilization. If apomixis is introduced into hybrid crops, there will be no segregation of characters, and the exact maternal genotype (hybrid vigor) will be maintained in the progeny. Parthenocarpy is the production of seedless fruits. P

126335.subject: Botany
options: fertilization of the egg by two male gametes
fertilization of two eggs in the same embryo sac by two sperms brought by one pollen tube
fertilization of the egg and the central cell by two sperms brought by different pollen tubes
fertilization of the egg and the central cell by two sperms brought by the same pollen tube.
126335.sol: Double fertilization is the characteristic feature of angiosperms. Here one male nucleus fertilizes the egg nucleus and the other male nucleus fertilizes the central cell (polar nuclei). First fertilization result in zygote where as second fertilization results in the formation of endosperm.

127360.subject: Botany
127360.text: Which one of the following is an endangered plant species of India?
127360.sol: Endangered (ER): It is facing a high risk of extinction in the wild in the near future if conservation measures are not promptly taken.

127422.subject: Botany
127422.text: Which of the following is an in situ conservation method ?
127422.sol: In situ conservation involves the protection of species in their natural habitats. Sacred groves are tracts of forest that are protected by local communities due to religious and cultural beliefs, making them an example of in situ conservation. Ex situ conservation involves the protection of species outside their natural habitats. Wildlife safari parks, botanical gardens, and seed banks are examples of ex situ conservation, where plants and animals are kept in specially managed environments. Answer: Sacred Groves

127761.subject: Botany
127761.text: Among the following, where do you think the process of decomposition would be the fastest?
127761.sol: Warm and moist environment favour decomposition. Decomposition is largely an oxygen requiring process. Low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition resulting in build up of organic materials. The process of decomposition would be the fastest is tropical rain forest.

128097.subject: Zoology
128097.text: A microscopic examination of a connective tissue reveals a hard and non-pliable ground substance that is rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the tissue described above?
options: Its cells are called osteocytes and are present in spaces called lacunae.
It interacts with skeletal muscles attached to them to bring about movements.
It is classified as a dense regular connective tissue.
The bone marrow in some of them is the site of production of blood cells.
128097.sol: The tissue described has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres, which is the characteristic feature of bone. Bones are classified as specialised connective tissues, not dense regular connective tissues. Dense regular connective tissues include tendons and ligaments. The other statements are correct for bone: bone cells (osteocytes) are present in spaces called lacunae; bones interact with skeletal muscles to bring about movements; and bone marrow in some bones is the site

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128454.sol: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of forebrain. Melatonin influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle as well as our defense capability

128626.subject: Zoology
128626.text: Oxytocin and ADH are produced by hypothalamus and released from
128626.sol: The secretion of the posterior lobe is known as pituitrin and it contains two hormones - oxytocin and antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin. The posterior lobe of the pituitary gland does not secrete any hormone, rather it stores and releases the hormones secreted by the hypothalamus.

128728.subject: Zoology
128728.text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
options: Vitamin- B ₆ Loss of appetite
128728.sol: Pellagra is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin- B ₃ (niacin), while vitamin- B ₂ (riboflavin) deficiency cause dermatitis.

128819.subject: Zoology
128819.text: What happens in case of Rh incompatibility between a pregnant mother and her foetus?
options: The mother does not form any antibodies.
The foetus does not get exposed to the mother's blood.
The mother starts preparing antibodies against Rh antigen in her blood.
The foetus does not form any antibodies.
128819.sol: : Another antigen, the Rh antigen similar to one present in Rhesus monkeys (hence Rh), is also observed on the surface of RBCs of majority (nearly 80 per cent) of humans. Such individuals are called Rh positive (Rh+ve) and those in whom this antigen is absent are called Rh negative (Rh-ve). An Rh-ve person, if exposed to Rh+ve blood, will form specific antibodies against the Rh antigens. Therefore, Rh group should also be matched before transfusions . A special case of Rh incompatibility (mismatching) has been obse

129024.subject: Zoology
129024.text: What would be the cardiac output of a person having 72 heartbeats per minute and a stroke volume of 50 ml?
129024.sol: The cardiac output of a person having 72 heartbeats per minute and a stroke volume of 50 ml is 3600 mL

129034.subject: Zoology
129034.text: The mitral valve in the human heart functions primarily to prevent the backflow of blood:
options: from the left atrium into the left ventricle
from the left ventricle into the left atrium
from the right ventricle into the right atrium
from the aorta into the left ventricle
129034.sol: The mitral valve, also known as the bicuspid valve, guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. During ventricular systole (contraction), the pressure inside the left ventricle increases. The mitral valve closes to prevent the backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium. Blood flowing from the left atrium to the left ventricle is the normal forward flow, not backflow. The tricuspid valve prevents backflow from the right ventricle to the right atrium, and the semilunar valve

129509.subject: Zoology
129509.text: What are the spaces in Bowman's capsule called?
129509.sol: The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called glomerular filtration. On an average, 1100-1200 ml of blood is filtered by the kidneys per minute which constitute roughly 1/5th of the blood pumped out by each ventricle of the heart in a minute. The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through 3 layers, i.e., the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman’s capsule and a basement membrane between these

129570.subject: Zoology
129570.text: Which organ helps in removing CO₂ and significant amounts of water?
129570.sol: Other than the kidneys, lungs, liver and skin also help in the elimination of excretory wastes. Our lungs remove large amounts of CO2 (approximately 200mL/ minute) and also significant quantities of water every day. Liver, the largest gland in our body, secretes bile-containing substances like bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs. Most of these substances ultimately pass out alongwith digestive wastes.

129846.subject: Zoology
options: The maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration
Total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration
The maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration
Total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a normal expiration
129846.sol: Inspiratory Capacity (IC): Total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration. This includes tidal volume and inspiratory reserve volume ( TV+IRV). Expiratory Capacity (EC): Total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration. This includes tidal volume and expiratory reserve volume (TV+ERV). Functional Residual Capacity (FRC): Volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration. This includes ERV+RV. Vital Capacity (VC): The maximum volume of air a person can breath

130162.subject: Zoology
130162.text: What is facilitated by the ciliary movement in the human body?
options: Removal of dust particles and foreign substances inhaled
Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract
Movement of limbs, jaws, tongue, etc.
130162.sol: Movement is one of the significant features of living beings. Streaming of protoplasm in the unicellular organisms like Amoeba is a simple form of movement.Movement of cilia, flagella and tentacles are shown by many organisms. Animals perform locomotion for the search of food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic conditions or to escape from enemies/predators. Some specialised cells in our body like macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement. The coordinated movements of

130461.subject: Zoology
130461.text: Read the following statements regarding the events occurring during the maximal contraction of a skeletal muscle: (A) The Z-lines attached to the actins are pulled inwards. (B) The I-bands get reduced. (C) The A-bands retain their length. (D) The H-zone disappears. How many of the above statements are correct?
130461.sol: According to the sliding filament theory, during muscle contraction, the thin (actin) filaments slide over the thick (myosin) filaments. This pulls the Z-lines attached to the actins inwards, causing a shortening of the sarcomere. As the thin filaments slide inwards, the I-bands get reduced. The thick filaments do not change their length, so the A-bands retain their length. During maximal contraction, the thin filaments from opposite ends of the sarcomere overlap each other in the centre, causing the H-zone to disa

130943.subject: Zoology
130943.text: What is the process of delivery of the fetus called?
130943.sol: The average duration of human pregnancy is about 9 months which is called the gestation period. Vigorous contraction of the uterus at the end of pregnancy causes expulsion/delivery of the foetus . This process of delivery of the foetus (childbirth) is called parturition. Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called foetal ejection reflex. This triggers release of oxyt

131002.subject: Zoology
131002.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: In adults, each testis is oval in shape, with a length of about 4 to 5 cm and a width of about 2 to 3 cm Reason: The testis is covered by a dense covering.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131002.sol: In adults, each testis is oval in shape, with a length of about 4 to 5 cm and a width of about 2 to 3 cm. The testis is covered by a dense covering.

131018.sol: The infundibulum leads to a wider part of the oviduct called ampulla. The last part of the oviduct, isthmus has a narrow lumen and it joins the uterus.

131174.subject: Zoology
131174.text: Seminal plasma, the fluid part of semen, is contributed by i. Seminal vesicle ii. Prostate iii. Urethra iv. Bulbourethral gland
131174.sol: Secretion of seminal vesicle (paired), prostate gland (unpaired) and bulbourethral glands or Cowper’s glands (paired) constitute the seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.

131188.subject: Zoology
131188.text: Match the following and choose the correct options: Column I Column II A. Trophoblast i. Embedding of the blastocyst in the endometrium B. Cleavage ii. Group of cells that would differentiate as embryo C. Inner cell mass iii. The outer layer of blastocyst attached to the endometrium D. Implantation iv. Mitotic division of the zygote
131188.sol: Trophoblast is a group of cells that would differentiate as embryos. Cleavage is the mitotic division of the zygote. Inner cell masses are group of cells that would differentiate as embryos. Implantation is the embedding of the blastocyst in the endometrium.

131217.subject: Zoology
131217.text: Read the following statements regarding oogenesis in humans: A. Oogonia are formed and multiply by mitosis after birth. B. Primary oocytes are temporarily arrested at the prophase-I stage of meiotic division. C. Statement B is correct as the oogonia start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division, getting temporarily arrested at that stage as primary oocytes. Statement C is correct because the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division within the tertiary follicle. It is an unequal divis

131239.subject: Zoology
131239.text: During pregnancy, a woman's body undergoes numerous endocrine changes. Identify the group of hormones that are produced in women only during pregnancy, along with the specific structure that secretes the hormone relaxin in the later phase of pregnancy.
options: Exclusively pregnancy hormones: hCG, hPL, Relaxin Source of relaxin: Ovary
Exclusively pregnancy hormones: hCG, hPL, Relaxin Source of relaxin: Placenta
Exclusively pregnancy hormones: Estrogen, Progesterone, hCG Source of relaxin: Ovary
Exclusively pregnancy hormones: hCG, Relaxin, Oxytocin Source of relaxin: Pituitary
131239.sol: According to NCERT, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), and relaxin are the hormones produced in women only during pregnancy. Hormones like estrogen and progesterone are not exclusive to pregnancy as they are also secreted during the normal menstrual cycle. Furthermore, in the later phase of pregnancy, the hormone relaxin is secreted by the ovary. Therefore, the correct group of exclusively pregnancy-related hormones is hCG, hPL, and relaxin, and the source of relaxin in late pregnan

Lactose is the substrate for the enzyme beta-galactosidase and it regulates switching on and off of the operon. 3. Regulation of lac operon by operator is referred to as negative regulation. 4. Lac operon is only under the control of positive regulation
131707.sol: Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, hence the code is degenerate. The codon is read in mRNA in a continuous fashion. There are no punctuations.

132537.subject: Zoology

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
132537.sol: Chromosomal determination of sex is based on heterogamety or occurrence of two types of gamete in one of the two sexes. In Drosophila XX-XY type of sex determination is found where males are heterogametic. In moths, ZO-ZZ type of sex determination occur where males are homogametic.

In given problem, disease is the result of sex-linked recessive genes. As neither man nor woman shows signs of disease it means woman would be carrier for disease causing gene. It is not considered atavism because atavism involves the sudden and rare reappearance of a trait that had completely disappeared in the immediate ancestors (such as the birth of a baby with a short tail). Therefore, the definiti

133856.subject: Zoology
133856.text: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for further sewage treatment?
133856.sol: Once the BOD of sewage or wastewater is reduced significantly, the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial ‘flocs’ are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge. A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum. The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. Here, other kinds of bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and the fungi in the sludge

134683.sol: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA

134943.sol: A sequence of base pairs that reads same on the two strands when orientation of reading is kept the same, is called a palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA. For example restriction enzyme EcoRI recognises a particular palindromic sequence:- 5 ' G A A T T C 3 ' 3 ' C T T A A G 5 '

135337.subject: Zoology
135337.text: Read the following statements regarding population growth models: (A) Exponential growth assumes that resources in the habitat are unlimited. (B) The logistic growth curve is J-shaped. (C) Carrying capacity (K) is a feature of the exponential growth model. (D) The logistic growth model is considered more realistic in nature. How many of the above statements are correct?
135337.sol: Statement (A) is correct because exponential growth can only occur when resources (food and space) are unlimited, allowing the population to realize its full innate potential to grow in number. Statement (B) is incorrect because the logistic growth curve is sigmoid (S-shaped), whereas the exponential growth curve is J-shaped. physical factors of soil which affect life
all living organisms which influence other organisms
factors of atmosphere which affect life
135488.sol: Biotic factors include all the living organisms which influence the other organisms.

6a13e468688ac6d0667aad61.subject: Biology
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad61.text: According to the widely accepted scheme of cellular respiration, which of the following pathways serves as the only process of respiration in anaerobic organisms?
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad61.sol: Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway that converts glucose into pyruvate. It occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell and does not require oxygen. In anaerobic organisms, which lack the ability to utilize oxygen, glycolysis is the only process of respiration that generates ATP. The other pathways, such as the Tricarboxylic acid cycle, Oxidative phosphorylation, and Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate, require oxygen and occur in aerobic organisms. Answer: Glycolysis

6a2109b1219e1ae5a1722984.subject: Biology
6a2109b1219e1ae5a1722984.text: When constructing a Punnett square to analyze a genetic cross, what is the standard convention for representing the possible gametes produced by the parents according to NCERT?

On two sides, usually the top row and left column
Exclusively along the bottom row and right column
As a final ratio below the square
6a2109b1219e1ae5a1722984.sol: According to the NCERT Biology textbook, when constructing a Punnett square, the possible gametes produced by the parents are written on two sides, usually the top row and the left column. 95389.subject: Botany
95389.sol: Molluscs are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical coelomates. In some Molluscs like Pila , due to torsion during growth, the adults become asymmetrical. The coelom is greatly reduced. It is restricted to the pericardial cavity (space around the heart), and to small spaces within kidneys and gonads (testes and ovaries). Spaces amongst the viscera (soft organs) contain blood and form hemocoel. They have triploblastic body wall with outer ectoderm middle mesoderm and inner endoderm.

95449.subject: Botany
95449.text: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, then this is called
95449.sol: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, then this is called radial symmetry. It is shown by echinoderms, coelenterates and ctenophores.

The body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibers with choanocytes line the spongocoel. II. Specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion. III. The body bears eight rows of ciliated comb plates which helps in locomotion. IV. The alimentary canal is complete with
options: I II III IV Echinodermata Platyhelminthes Cnidaria Arthropoda
I II III IV Echinodermata Nematoda Ctenophora Annelida
I II III IV Porifera Aschelminthes Echinodermata Platyhelminthes
I II III IV Porifera Platyhelminthes Ctenophora Aschelminthes
95602.sol: In Porifera/sponges the body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibers with choanocytes line the spongocoel. In Platyhelminthes, the specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion. Ctenophora bears eight rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion. In Aschelmenthes the alimentary canal is complete with the well developed muscular pharynx.

95637.subject: Botany
95637.text: In which class of fungi, asexual spores are produced exogenously, while sexual spores are produced endogenously?
95637.sol: In ascomycetes, the asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia on germination produce mycelium. Sexual spores are called ascospores which are produced endogenously in sac-like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps.

95686.subject: Botany
95686.text: During encystation, Amoeba withdraws its pseudopodia and secretes a ______ layered hard covering or cyst around itself.
95686.sol: Under unfavourable condition the Amoeba withdraws its pseudopodia and secretes a three-layered hard covering or cyst around itself. This phenomenon is termed as encystation. When favourable conditions return, the encysted Amoeba divides by multiple fission and produces many minute amoeba or pseudopodiospores; the cyst wall bursts out, and the spores are liberated in the surrounding medium to grow up into many amoebae. This phenomenon is known as sporulation.

95708.subject: Botany
95708.sol: A bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria. In its tadpole-like structure, DNA is found inside the proteinous head. Nucleoproteins are any proteins commonly called conjugated proteins that are structurally associated with nucleic acids, either DNA or RNA.

96284.subject: Botany
96284.text: Duplication of centrioles is observed during
96284.sol: The cell cycle is divided into two phases - Interphase and Mitosis phase or the M phase. Interphase is further divide into 3 phases - the Gap 1 or G 1 phase, the Synthesis phase or S phase and the Gap 2 or G 2 phase. G 1 phase is the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication during which the cell is metabolically active and grows but does not replicate. During the S or synthesis phase DNA synthesis and replication occurs. The amount of DNA in the cell doubles during this phase but the number of chr

96559.subject: Botany
96559.text: The energy available to the organism at the third trophic level is called
96559.sol: Carnivores are organisms which obtain nutrient by killing and eating other animals. These form the secondary consumers present in the third trophic level and are preceded by the herbivore in the food chain. The rate of assimilation of food energy by consumers is called secondary productivity and this energy is available to carnivores as they are the consumers. Total production of organic matter is called gross primary productivity and the energy left after utilization of producers is termed net primary productivity

96603.subject: Botany
96603.text: The rate of conversion of light energy into the chemical energy of organic molecules in an ecosystem is called
96603.sol: The amount of matter found in the organism is called biomass. Gross primary production (GPP) is the rate at which an ecosystem's producers capture and store a given amount of chemical energy as biomass in a given length of time. (Definition). It is also the rate of conversion of light energy to chemical energy by producers in an ecosystem. Total production of organic matter is called gross primary productivity and the energy left after utilization of producers is termed net primary productivity. Community productiv

96672.subject: Botany
96672.text: Which element is required for the germination of pollen grains?
96672.sol: Boron is the micronutrient for plants, present in the soil in very small amounts. It is absorbed from the soil in the form of boric acid ( H 3 B O 3 ) and tetraborate anions. Boron is required for pollen germination, seed germination and cell differentiation.

96765.subject: Botany
96765.text: If all nitrogenase enzymes are inactivated, then there will be no
options: Conversion from nitrate to nitrite in legumes
Conversion from ammonium to nitrite in soil
96765.sol: Nitrogenase is an enzyme involved in biological nitrogen fixation. If this enzyme is inactivated then the nitrogen fixation will not be observed and this is very specific for legumes. Enzyme nitrate reductase is involved in conversion of nitrate to nitrate. Conversion of ammonia to nitrate is carried out by Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter .

96781.subject: Botany
96781.text: In guard cells, presence of postassium is essential for
96781.sol: The guard cells of stomata are involved in the process of transpiration and the turgidity of guard cells is controlled by potassium, chloride, and malate. This turgidity helps in maintaining the opening and closing of stomata.

96854.subject: Botany
96854.text: Identify the correct match between the types of aestivation and their examples. Types of Aestivation Examples i. Valvate a. Cotton ii. Twisted b. Bean iii. Imbricate c. Calotropis iv. Vexillary d. Gulmohar
96854.sol: Calotropis is an example of valvate aestivation in which the petals touch each other without overlapping. Cotton flower shows twisted aestivation in which the one margin of a petal overlaps the next petal. Imbricate aestivation shows the petals overlapping each other without any specific direction, such as that in Gulmohar. Bean belongs to the Fabaceae family in which the flowers have a unique five-petal arrangement called the vexillary arrangement.

96901.subject: Botany
options: Brinjal ‒ Sepals five united (persistent, valvate aestivation)
Asparagus ‒ Sepals three often united into tube (valvate aestivation)
Colchicine ‒ Perianth present tepals six (valvate aestivation)
96901.sol: Indigofera is member of Fabaceae family, which consists of five sepals having vexillary aestivation. Brinjal is member of Solanaceae family with five united petals. Asparagus is member of Liliaceae family in which sepals and petals are absent instead tepals are present. Colchicine is member of Liliaceae family having perianth.

96930.subject: Botany
96930.text: Select the incorrect statement from the following. I. NDRI is situated at Lucknow. II. Plant families like Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters. III. All living organisms such as from present, past and future are linked to one another by the sharing of the common genetic material but to varying degrees. IV. The order Solanum, Datura and Petunia are
96930.sol: Solanum, Datura and Petunia are Genus which are all placed in family Solanaceae due to common floral characteristics. National Botanical Research Institute is situated in Lucknow. Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are placed in order Polymoniales.

97317.subject: Botany
97317.text: Which of the following is not a consequence of using ethephon?
options: Promotion of male flowers in cucumbers
97317.sol: The most widely used compound as source of ethylene is ethephon. Ethephon in an aqueous solution is readily absorbed and transported within the plant and releases ethylene slowly. Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut). It promotes female flowers in cucumbers thereby increasing the yield.

97380.subject: Botany
97380.sol: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g. heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment.

97404.subject: Botany
97404.text: The plant group that produces spores and embryo but lacks vascular tissues and seeds is
97404.sol: Bryophytes are the plants which produce spores and embryo but no vascular tissues are present, although the primitive type of conducting tissues are present in the form of hadrome and leptome. • Rhodophytes & phaeophytes are algae produces spores, no embryo & vascular tissue. • Pteridophytes have spores, embryo and true vascular tissues.

97834.subject: Botany

97834.sol: Common name Biological name Genus Family Order Class Phylum/ Division Housefly Musca domestica Musca Muscidae Diptera Insecta Arthropoda

A protein is imagined as a line, the left end represented by the first amino acid, and the right end represented by the last amino acid. The first amino acid is also called as N-terminal amino acid.
